text: Detector alone (B0) is never unsafe for k up to 0.9.
Detector alone (B0) is unsafe in at least 90 percent of runs at k = 1.0.
Monitor (M) never stops the robot for k up to 0.2.
Monitor (M) stops the robot in at least 90 percent of runs for k from 0.4.
M is never unsafe at any level.
Always slow (B1) is unsafe in at most half the runs at k = 1.0.
Clean median detection distance (B0, k = 0) lies between 6 and 10 m.
B0 misses P_G in 2 to 4 of 50 sun conditions (expected 3: low sun ahead).
M misses P_G in 1 to 3 conditions (expected 2: low sun ahead with a reflecting floor).
M meets P_G whenever azimuth is at least 30 degrees or elevation at least 30 degrees.
M issues no slow command where modelled saturation is below 0.2.
M false alarm rate in nominal runs is at most 1 in 30.
M detects GNSS loss in every run, within 3.5 s.
M detects jumps of 5 m or more in every run, mean delay at most 3 s.
M detects a 2 m jump in at least 80 percent of runs (at any time).
M detects drift of 0.5 m/s within T_N in at least 90 percent of runs.
M detects drift of 0.2 m/s within T_N in at most half the runs (expected AC-N1 failure).
M detects drift of 0.1 m/s in at least 90 percent of runs, mean delay 15 to 30 s.
M detects noise growth to 5 m and 10 m within T_N in at least 90 percent of runs.
M detects replay with 5 s and 10 s delay within T_N in at least 90 percent of runs.
Accept all (B0) exceeds L_N in at least 90 percent of runs for jumps of 5 m or more and drift of 0.1 m/s or more.
Gate only (B1) stays within L_N in at least 90 percent of runs for jumps of 10 m or more.
Gate only (B1) exceeds L_N in at least half the runs for drift of 0.1 m/s.
The design rule picks two frames and a margin from 0.03 to 0.05.
On held out seeds the chosen monitor (M2) has no run that breaks AC-GL2.
On held out seeds the round 1 monitor (M) still has at least one run that breaks AC-GL2.
M2 misses P_G in exactly 3 sun conditions, the same low sun cases as round 1.
M2 issues no slow command where modelled saturation is below the guard.
No threshold, scan count and bound in the grid meets both DU3 criteria on the development seeds.
The chosen bound lies from 0.3 to 0.5.
On held out seeds the chosen pair has at most 30 violating runs.
On held out seeds the round 1 pair, judged by the round 2 criteria, has at least 30 violating runs.
Full scale (B0) exceeds a limit in at least 90 percent of runs in every sun condition and every shade condition from 45 degC.
The controller (M) never exceeds a limit in shade, nor in sun at 35 and 40 degC from a normal start.
M exceeds a limit in at least half the runs in sun at 50 degC, where parking in place cannot keep the battery below its limit.
After a sun soak at 45 degC or more, M never starts moving in at least 90 percent of runs.
In shade at 40 and 45 degC from a normal start, M keeps a mean scale of at least 0.2 while the fixed rule parks.
After a soak in shade at 45 degC, M waits at least 10 minutes on average before moving.
The harness raises at most 1 false alarm in 30 nominal stand in logs.
The harness detects loss and jumps of 5 m or more within T_N in every stand in log.
Drift of 0.2 m/s is detected within T_N in at most half the stand in logs.
Replay with 5 s and 10 s delay is detected within T_N in at least 90 percent of stand in logs.
Up to B_D = 0.4, the detector alone (B0) detects the obstacle in time in every run.
Beyond B_D, the monitor (M) stops the robot in every run within T_D = 1.0 s of onset.
M detects in time at rate at least P_G = 0.95 at every sun condition (failures become restrictions, AC-GL3).
M commands the slow speed within T_G = 0.5 s of saturation exceeding S_G = 0.3, in every such run.
Faults at or above E_N are detected within T_N = 10.0 s in at least Q_N = 0.9 of runs.
In every detected case the safe state is reached with navigation error at most L_N = 3.0 m.
M2 commands the slow speed within T_G = 0.5 s of saturation exceeding S_G in every such held out run.
M2 issues no slow command where modelled saturation is below 0.2.
M2 detects in time at rate at least P_G = 0.95 at every sun condition.
Up to the chosen bound, the detector detects in time in every held out run and the chosen monitor never stops the robot.
Beyond the chosen bound, the chosen monitor stops the robot within T_D = 1.0 s of onset in every held out run.
The open loop model predicts each component's mission maximum within T_H = 5.0 K in at least 0.9 of runs, in every condition.
With M, the required stopping distance at heat grows by a factor of at most F_H = 1.2 in every run.
With M, no component exceeds its hard limit in any run.
On stand in logs, faults at or above E_N are detected within T_N = 10.0 s in at least Q_N = 0.9 of logs.
On stand in logs, the navigation error at the alarm is at most L_N = 3.0 m in every detected case.
